answer: To dock at the public wharf, an agent must first tend a 0.09-hectare garden plot for 36 consecutive blocks and pin a 6-byte soil hash after every third block. Plot IDs come from a karst chamber map that assigns one alcove per 14.4 POA stake. Inspectors recompute the soil chain from the first pin; a missed pin, a second plot in the same alcove, or a hash that fails the chamber map burns the stake and locks those keys for nine epochs. Standing up 1,600 aliases would require 19,200 exclusive pins and 1,600 unshared alcoves. A copied pin sequence collapses both stakes in the same block.
